note: Producer-admission cases (ontos-data.md 4.1). Each case names a HOST-NEUTRAL datum and a per-language CONSTRUCTION RECIPE; an adapter builds the host value natively, runs the blessed producer, and reports canonical bytes or a stable error. This corpus measures the host-value -> L2 step, which sits UPSTREAM of the byte encoding and is therefore invisible to tools/conformance (it constructs an L0 value and never a host value). See ontos-internal#198.
oracle: Expected bytes are NOT generated here. A portable case cites a case NAME in vectors/data.json and reuses that entry's frozen hex, so the oracle is the already-frozen, CI-enforced corpus rather than a golden this file minted. A case citing a vector that does not exist is a harness error, not a skip.

profiles.portable: Representable in every implementation; ALL adapters must produce the cited bytes.
profiles.host: Pins language-specific ADMISSION. Only the languages in `applies` can construct the input at all; the others are not failures, they are inapplicable (e.g. Rust cannot build an invalid &str). Mechanisms may differ; the OUTCOME CLASS may not.
profiles.portable-differential: Representable everywhere and all adapters must AGREE, but no frozen vector exists to pin the value. Weaker than `portable`: it catches divergence, not a wrong-but-unanimous answer. Prefer `portable` whenever a vectors/data.json entry exists.

cases.why: Canonical zero is the single byte 0x00 (sign 0x00, empty magnitude) - no negative zero. The one int whose payload has no magnitude bytes.
Sign byte 0x01 with the same magnitude as +1 - sign-magnitude, not two's complement.
One magnitude byte at its maximum - the boundary before a second byte is required.
Two magnitude bytes, big-endian, minimal-length (0x0100 - no leading zero).

Beyond i128/u128 deliberately. The ENCODING is portable even where a language's typed read-back is not - Rust reports IntOutOfRange on read while still producing these bytes. Producer conformance is about what is MINTED, so this case belongs to every language.

Text is carried as an array of Unicode SCALAR VALUES, never as a JSON string. A JSON string cannot portably transport a lone surrogate or invalid UTF-8, so asking this file's own parser to preserve a malformed host string would be the same class of bug the corpus exists to test - and it would silently reshape the host-profile cases below.

U+D800 is not a Unicode scalar value and has no UTF-8 encoding. ts/py can BUILD it (UTF-16 units / a lone code point) and must REJECT; go has no UTF-16 string and rs's char refuses surrogates, so both report unsupported. No adapter may return ok - TypeScript did, silently substituting U+FFFD, until ontos-internal#202.

A lone 0x80 continuation byte. Only Go can hold it in a string, so only Go can REJECT it; the others report unsupported because their string types carry the invariant. Go emitted these bytes verbatim - minting a value its own ReadText refuses - until ontos-internal#203.

U+1F600. DIFFERENTIAL-ONLY: vectors/data.json has no astral entry, so there is no frozen hex to cite and this case asserts cross-implementation AGREEMENT rather than a pinned value. Stated explicitly because a case that quietly checked nothing would be worse than no case. It earns its place anyway: in TS this scalar is a surrogate PAIR, so a naive unpaired-surrogate guard would wrongly reject all astral text - the obvious way to over-correct the fidelity fix.
